100% (which is why we pointed it out).

We had to decide between waiting another 2-3 months (maybe more) to publish, or sending this and following up with the functional assays. We’re very upfront in the article about what was tested and what wasn’t. 

Not to beat a dead horse, but we are an investment research firm - not a biotech startup. The trade has been moving the entire time we were waiting for data, and we had enough insight from the experience thus far to write at least a first look. 

I’m equally as curious as everyone else as to the results of a patch clamp test - we spent months waiting for the binding and competition assays, of course we want to know if it neutralizes. 

But to be clear - even if we published a full in vitro study package ready to move to in vivo, people would say “well you don’t have tox/Pk/this that or the other animal” and then it would be “well showing in humans is the real constraint”. We don’t disagree with any of that, but our job isn’t to get an FDA approved medicine. It’s to do primary research and share a slightly better informed take - as it relates to the companies and technology - with our audience. 

I understand it would have been way cooler if it had the functional data. But it also could have meant significantly worse valuations to enter in on the names we like. And - final time - that’s our job. IMO it’s pretty damn cool we got the competitive binding, we’re not structural biologists (by any stretch of the imagination). But I understand the urge to nitpick!
